title: FedRAMP OSCAL September 30 mandate, explained
question: What is the FedRAMP OSCAL September 30 mandate?
answer: The FedRAMP Program Management Office requires System Security Plans (SSPs), and related authorization artifacts, to be authored in the Open Security Controls Assessment Language (OSCAL) machine-readable format, with the mandated transition target set for September 30. For an AI control plane that must hand its measured state to an authorizing official, the practical consequence is that risk posture has to be expressed as structured data, not prose: every control, every assessment result, every boundary statement has to be storable, comparable, and auditable by tooling. This is how a verified measurement credential plugs into FedRAMP: it is formatted for the machine review that the September 30 mandate makes unavoidable.
ref: Council of AI — FedRAMP/OSCAL machine-readable marking series (2026-08-14 build)
